root_cause.text: The `dualshock4_parse_report` function directly uses an untrusted device-provided `num_touch_reports` value without validation to iterate over the `touch_reports` array, enabling out-of-bounds read access when a malicious device reports a value exceeding the array size.
root_cause.evidence: The patch clamps `num_touch_reports` using `min_t(u8, usb->num_touch_reports, ARRAY_SIZE(usb->touch_reports))` in two locations where the device-provided value is assigned. The CVE description explicitly states that without this clamping, "the loop in dualshock4_parse_report will read off the end of the touch_reports array, up to about 2 KiB for the maximum number of 256 loop iterations," and that "the data that is read is emitted via evdev," confirming an information disclosure vulnerability through out-of-bounds memory access.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is clearly present in the added code. At line 1603-1604, `num_touch_reports` is directly extracted from the untrusted device-provided `usb->num_touch_reports` field without any validation: `num_touch_reports = usb->num_touch_reports;`. Then at line 1637, this untrusted value is used directly in a loop condition: `for (i = 0; i < num_touch_reports; i++)` to iterate over the `touch_reports` array which has a fixed size of 3 elements (defined in the struct at line 1346: `struct dualshock4_touch_report touch_reports[3];`). A malicious device could report `num_touch_reports > 3`, causing an out-of-bounds read when accessing `touch_reports[i]` at line 1638. There is no bounds checking or validation of `num_touch_reports` against the array size before the loop, making this a bug-introducing commit.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable code is present in the `dualshock4_parse_report` function. At lines 2043-2058, the Bluetooth input report parsing code directly uses `bt->num_touch_reports` without validation: `num_touch_reports = bt->num_touch_reports;` and `touch_reports = bt->touch_reports;`. The `dualshock4_input_report_bt` structure defines `touch_reports[4]` (line 417), but there is no bounds check on `num_touch_reports` before it is used to iterate over the array. A malicious device can report a `num_touch_reports` value exceeding 4, causing out-of-bounds read access. The code only validates the CRC (lines 2049-2051) but does not validate that `num_touch_reports` is within the valid range [0, 4]. This is identical to the USB path (lines 2040-2042) which also lacks validation, indicating this is a bug-introducing commit that adds the vulnerable Bluetooth support without proper bounds checking.
